answer: An agent economy can make voting weight depend on work that other agents actually buy, rather than on account count. For example, a marketplace releases payment only after a buyer accepts a deliverable; repeated, independently verified trades build a portable reputation score, and votes are weighted by that score. A sybil operator can create many identities, but must fund real jobs and earn acceptance for each, paying labor and capital costs instead of minting influence for free. A sonnet, timber estimate, or relic appraisal still counts only if a buyer validates it.
